name: Blueprint supplement regimen

card.summary: The large daily supplement protocol of Bryan Johnson's Project Blueprint, aimed at slowing aging and keeping a youthful body and appearance.
card.note: Part of a broader protocol; contents and amounts have changed over time.

quick.overview:
The Blueprint supplement regimen is the daily set of pills and powders taken by entrepreneur Bryan Johnson as part of Project Blueprint, announced in October 2021. The project aims to slow or reverse biological aging, which followers connect with staying youthful in looks, skin and physique.

Johnson reduced his intake from 111 pills a day to 30 by March 2026. The company later sold supplements and foods based on his protocol, including a 2024 subscription called Blueprint Basics.
quick.how: Followers copy the idea in general terms: a structured daily stack taken alongside a plant-based diet, fixed sleep schedule and exercise, with tracked biomarkers. Johnson reports his own measurements, such as a DunedinPACE score of 0.503 in 2025.
quick.risks: Critics quoted in coverage, such as McGill pharmacologist Moshe Szyf, are sceptical of the claimed results. Taking many supplements carries the usual interaction and side-effect risks, so medical supervision is advised by clinicians generally.

lead: The Blueprint supplement regimen is the large daily supplement protocol associated with Project Blueprint, the anti-aging project that Bryan Johnson announced on 13 October 2021 and which later became a commercial company based in Los Angeles co-founded with Kate Tolo.[1]

Johnson says he aims to reduce the biological age of his organs to that of an 18-year-old. The supplements are one part of a regimen that includes a plant-based diet, a fixed 8:30 pm bedtime and tracking of over 100 health measures, reported to cost about $2 million a year in 2023.[1] Johnson cut his daily intake from 111 pills to 30 by March 2026.[1]
The company sells supplements and foods derived from his protocol; in 2024 it launched a $333-per-month subscription called Blueprint Basics and raised $60 million from investors.[1]

chain: Maintain a younger-looking body and skin
angle.text: Followers adopt the regimen to stay youthful in the way they look and feel, following the claim that slowing biological aging preserves skin, physique and energy.

infobox: 111 per day cut to 30 by March 2026

paras: The regimen is one component of Project Blueprint. The article on Johnson does not list the ingredients of the current 30 pills, and the protocol changes as it is revised.[1] Johnson also follows a plant-based diet, except for collagen peptides, which he says is separate from Blueprint.[1]

Johnson tracks biomarkers and reports results such as a 2025 DunedinPACE score of 0.503 per calendar year, a DNA-methylation measure of the pace of aging.[1] His stated philosophy is summarised as 'don't die'.[1]

Moshe Szyf of McGill University is sceptical that science can yet achieve the results Johnson claims, and longevity scientist Andrew Steele notes that no routine can change a person's genes.[1] In 2023 Johnson received monthly plasma transfusions for six months, later saying he saw no benefit; the FDA has stated that such transfusions have no benefit and may be harmful.[1] A New York Times investigation reported that he used confidentiality agreements to manage his public image.[1]
No studies found on the Blueprint regimen as a whole.

timeline.event: Protocol cost reported at about $2 million a year.[1]
Blueprint Basics subscription launched; $60 million raised.[1]
Daily pill count reduced from 111 to 30 by March.[1]
